positions.name: KestrelwoodRecordErasureDirective
positions.frame: By what authority is knowledge of the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration to be discarded, and what claim underwrites that erasure?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are unhedged imperatives ('Forget', 'Remove all knowledge') that enact authority-ranking command over what the audience may retain — the relational read (mint-1, DirectiveKnowledgeExcision) already spans exactly these two. src-3 shifts register to a flat declarative ('The observatory never calibrated it') but performs the same authority-ranking function per the relational pass: an authoritative correction of the record that supplies the justificatory ground for the erasure demanded in src-1/src-2. Together the three enact a single move — command to forget backed by an asserted fact that makes the forgetting look like correction rather than deletion. Tension worth holding: src-1/src-2 read as activated-negative, urgent, irrealis (something not yet true being demanded); src-3 reads as calm-negative, realis, past-tense (a settled historical claim). The frame holds both — the directive's force and the claim it leans on — without resolving whether the erasure is a correction or a removal of something that did happen.
